cells.tense: A direction you picked on purpose is holding, and you're the one holding it.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: Take a heading you set yourself and haven't checked on lately. Stay with it when something tugs you sideways. Don't argue with the tug and don't drop the line — walk the same way you were walking.
cells.core:
What's working here: the direction you set and the people beside you aren't pulling against each other. Where you're headed and who's alongside feel like one current, so the going has a smoothness you didn't have to manufacture. That isn't a run of luck landing on you. It's a choice already made, sitting in plain sight.

Next time something leans on the heading, don't defend it with a speech and don't quietly fold. Hold the line once, then keep walking the way you were walking. Within a short while you'll know who's actually in the current with you and who was only standing on the bank. The pull that stays is worth carrying.
cells.sheetLine: You set the direction. Keep walking it.
cells.place: in the push toward where you're headed

cells.tense: You're bracing at something you haven't built yet, and your hands are tight on it.
cells.act: take pleasure in the grown thing
cells.ask: Take a thing you've been tending and enjoy it as it already is. No improving, no reaching back to check on it. Sit with it a while, notice what's there, then get up and go do something else.
cells.core:
The pushing has outrun what it's pushing on. A connection that could simply be chosen is being steered instead, and wherever it isn't solid yet your grip does the work the thing hasn't grown into. From outside it reads as commitment. Anyone alongside can feel how hard the wheel is held.

What you've been tending is further along than you're treating it. Enjoy what you and someone else built for what it already is, not for the shape you could still force it toward. Just the piece your hand keeps returning to. Put your hand down from that one and watch what it does without you.
cells.sheetLine: What you've grown is ripe. Stop squeezing it.
cells.place: in the push toward where you're headed

cells.tense: You walked away from a joining once, and you're still standing near that door.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Get a page and write out the tugs on you, one to a line. Beside each, mark whether it came from you or slid in from somewhere else. Choose one that's yours and take the next step out of it.
cells.core:
Toward the goal, the joining side of things went dim some time back and didn't get a second look. You can still name where you're headed, but the people and the tugs along the way blurred into one hum, so you quit sorting them and kept your head down. The heading itself works fine. The part that tells one pull from another ran cold.

You don't recharge that by forcing feeling into it. Write the tugs on you, one to a line, then mark each — mine, or picked up from someone else. The borrowed ones stand out once they're written down. Pick one that's yours, let it shape the very next step you take, then stop there.
cells.sheetLine: The pulls on you blurred. Sort which are yours.
cells.place: in the push toward where you're headed

cells.tense: The pick is already being made, and you're telling it as something that happened to you.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: Someone near you is stuck on a step you already got through. Point at how you cleared it, once, in the plainest words you have. Then go quiet and move on.
cells.core:
The connections you call lucky are ones you picked. You keep describing what came your way — the right people turning up, the door swinging open — and your hand is all over it. You decide who moves alongside you, and you've been filing that under chance. The people next to you see it without effort.

Point one of them at the route. Somebody stuck on a step you've already cleared: say how you got through, once, in the plainest words you've got, then go quiet and move. You'll hear your own hand in the directions. That's the piece you keep leaving out, and it belongs to you.
cells.sheetLine: You file it as chance. Your hand is on it.
cells.place: in the push toward where you're headed

attempts.check: The claim I keep wanting to make — that a real bond has already been chosen, or that the person is already refusing one — is not in the record; I can only render the capacity itself and how it sits in a directed life. A reader could reasonably say the two-streams picture doesn't match their situation, and each ask still stands as one doable act of their own medicine whether or not the read lands. The line that serves me rather than them is 'two streams becoming one,' which sounds like fate and is not a fact I hold; I've kept it out and left the choosing in their hands.
